tldr: Claude Opus 5.5 and Sonnet 5.5 reached Google Antigravity on Oct 20, giving developers a per-task model choice inside an agentic IDE. Three days later R&D World set Moonshot's Kimi K3.1 Pro against Opus 5.5 and GPT-6 Astra, making Opus 5.5 the reference point for open-weight challengers.
whats_new: Anthropic's Nov 9 guide compares Fable, Opus, Sonnet and Haiku on cost and use, and shows how to combine them, so model routing is now documented first-party guidance.
why_it_matters: Opus 5.5 is both the model teams route to and the yardstick Kimi K3.1 Pro is measured against, so tiering and challenger evals now rest on the same baseline.

status.detail: The thread now spans Opus 5.5 distribution, a Kimi K3.1 Pro comparison against it, and Anthropic's own model-selection guidance; the items here do not report independent eval results.

beats.headline: Opus 5.5 and Sonnet 5.5 arrive in Google Antigravity
beats.summary: Google Cloud positions the pair as different models for different tasks, from quick bug fixes to complex migrations.

beats.headline: Kimi K3.1 Pro set against Opus 5.5 and GPT-6 Astra
beats.summary: R&D World frames a head-to-head; only the headline is in the item, so results are unconfirmed here.

beats.headline: Anthropic publishes a guide to choosing among Fable, Opus, Sonnet and Haiku
beats.summary: The post covers which model to pick, what each costs, and how to use them together.

open_questions: Do independent evals show Kimi K3.1 Pro matching Opus 5.5 on coding or agent tasks?
What per-token prices does the Nov 9 guide give for each Claude tier, and how do they compare with Kimi K3.1 Pro hosts?
Does the guide recommend a concrete routing split, such as planner on one tier and workers on another?
take_for_builders: Read Anthropic's Nov 9 tiering guide against your current routing, and rerun your own evals on Opus 5.5 versus Kimi K3.1 Pro before moving any traffic, since the comparison item reports no verified results.
